title: Machining mesh refuses the Solidcraft sample body at every chord (deviation ~2.8x the tolerance)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Found while working #1456 (Solidcraft `.sc` import, kernel side).

The final body of the maintainer's sample design (`testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc`, added on the #1456 branch) imports through `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::import_solidcraft` as a checked solid (volume > 0, the port's box is exactly the design's [-62.5, 62.5] x [-62.5, 62.5] x [0, 85] mm). But `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh::machining_mesh` refuses it at every chord tried, always by the deviation verdict:

| chord (mm) | refusal |
|---|---|
| 0.005 | face 50 stands 6.847e-3 mm off its surface |
| 0.01 | face 1 stands 2.348e-2 mm off its surface |
| 0.02 | face 36 stands 6.146e-2 mm off its surface |
| 0.05 | face 36 stands 1.337e-1 mm off its surface |
| 0.1 | face 36 stands 2.820e-1 mm off its surface |

The measured deviation grows with the chord at about 2.8x it, so the planner is not honouring the tolerance on some faces of this body (blends and a tilted cut plane: features 12-19 of the design). The refusal is the right outcome (Prime Directive), but it means the body cannot be machined once the app is wired to the import.

Reproduce: on the #1456 branch, import the sample with `import_solidcraft` and call `machining_mesh(&solid, tol, &CancelToken::new())`.

Done means: the sample's final body meshes at the app chord (0.005 mm) inside tolerance, or the faces that cannot are named with why, pinned by a test on the sample.

Related: #1029 (crafted records for every solidcore-tess shortfall), #940.
